title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 9
statement: Let \(x\) and \(y\) be two distinct roots of unity. Prove that \(x+y\) is also a root of unity if and only if \(\frac{y}{x}\) is a cube root of unity.

solutions.text: This is easiest to see geometrically. The vectors corresponding to \(x, y\), and \(-x-y\) sum to 0 , so they form a triangle. In order for them all to be roots of unity, they must all have length one, so the triangle must be equilateral. Therefore the angle between \(x\) and \(y\) is \(\pm \frac{2 \pi}{3}\), that is, \(\frac{y}{x}\) is a cube root of unity.
